note: Reference data only. Phone NFC reads 13.56 MHz (ISO 14443 / 15693 / 18092). 125 kHz credentials are listed for identification, they cannot be read by a phone.

cards.name: MIFARE Classic 1K
cards.notes: Clonable with a phone in seconds. Still used by hotels, gyms, older offices and some transit systems.

cards.name: MIFARE Classic 4K
cards.notes: Same weakness as 1K. Sectors 0-31 are 4 blocks, 32-39 are 16 blocks.

cards.name: MIFARE Ultralight
cards.notes: Event tickets, single-use passes. No cryptographic protection.

cards.name: MIFARE Ultralight C
cards.notes: Adds 3DES mutual authentication. Legacy 3DES is considered weak today.

cards.name: NTAG213
cards.notes: The most common sticker tag. NDEF URL/ text payloads.

cards.name: NTAG215
cards.notes: Amiibo-compatible size. Common in access-control stickers.

cards.name: NTAG216
cards.notes: Largest NTAG. Often used for vCard and Wi-Fi sharing tags.

cards.name: MIFARE DESFire EV1
cards.notes: Solid when AES is used. Legacy DES mode is the weak point.

cards.name: MIFARE DESFire EV2
cards.notes: Adds transaction MAC and proximity verification against relay attacks.

cards.name: MIFARE DESFire EV3
cards.notes: Current generation for corporate badges and campus cards.

cards.name: MIFARE Plus
cards.notes: Drop-in Crypto1 replacement. Once switched to SL3 it is not clonable.

cards.name: ICODE SLIX (ISO 15693)
cards.notes: Longer read range (up to ~1 m). Library books, laundry tags, industrial asset labels.

cards.name: FeliCa
cards.notes: Japan / Hong Kong transit and payment. Many phones can read it but not emulate it.

cards.name: Calypso
cards.notes: Transit standard in France, Belgium, Portugal, Brazil, Egypt and others.

cards.name: Visa contactless
cards.notes: PAN and expiry are readable without authentication; the cryptogram is not replayable.

cards.name: Mastercard contactless
cards.notes: Same EMV flow as Visa, different AID and application template.

cards.name: American Express contactless
cards.notes: Amex Pay / ExpressPay application.

cards.name: UnionPay QuickPass
cards.notes: China mainland debit/credit contactless.

cards.name: JCB contactless
cards.notes: Japan-issued cards, also accepted across Asia.

cards.name: MIR contactless
cards.notes: Russian domestic payment scheme.

cards.name: HID iCLASS / iCLASS SE
cards.notes: Corporate badges. Legacy iCLASS (non-SE) keys have been recovered publicly, SE is not affected.

cards.name: HID Seos
cards.notes: Not clonable with a phone. Often paired with iCLASS for migration.

cards.name: LEGIC advant
cards.notes: Common in European building access and time clocks.

cards.name: HID Prox (125 kHz)
cards.notes: Older office fobs. NOT readable by a phone: needs a 125 kHz coil (Flipper Zero, Proxmark).

cards.name: EM4100 / EM4102 (125 kHz)
cards.notes: Trivially clonable with cheap hardware, but again: not via phone NFC.

cards.name: China City Union card (住建部)
cards.security: Mixed — legacy Crypto1 in older issues
cards.notes: Older city bus cards are MIFARE Classic inside. Newer issues moved to CPU cards.

cards.name: China T-Union (交通联合)
cards.notes: National intercity transit card. Modern issues are not clonable.

cards.name: Troika / social cards
cards.notes: Representative of modern transit migrations: MIFARE Classic → Plus/DESFire.

cards.name: Hotel room key (RFID)
cards.notes: Many chains still ship MIFARE Classic with per-hotel keys. Check the SAK before assuming.

cards.name: NFC Forum Type 1
cards.notes: Rare today. Read/write with NDEF.

cards.name: NFC Forum Type 3
cards.notes: FeliCa-based tags used in Japan.

cards.name: NFC Forum Type 4
cards.notes: Smart posters, ticketing, passports' contactless interface.

cards.name: ePassport (ICAO 9303)
cards.notes: Readable only with the MRZ key printed inside the document. Not a cloning target.

cards.name: NFC ring / implant
cards.notes: Usually just an NTAG213 in resin — behaves exactly like a sticker.

cards.name: amiibo
cards.notes: NTAG215 with a locked data page. Can be cloned to a blank NTAG215.

cards.name: Tesla key card
cards.notes: Unlocked by the car, not by the card. Cloning the UID alone does nothing.

cards.name: DESFire transit ticket
cards.notes: Typical for new deployments in Europe and Asia.
